status: UNCOMPILED native Node timer/immediate Source; production defaultOFF. No engine/runtime/queue/drop/Store proof supplied.
moduleContract: Exact pinned namespace names, mutable CJS defaults/globals, native Engine queue and owned TimerTask. Immediate uses actual IMMEDIATE_TASK_HANDLE, not Promise or setTimeout alias.

node:timers.callablePolicy: Real native guest task ownership/refcounts/ALS capture; declared unsupported functions throw immediate own ERR_SM_NODE_UNSUPPORTED on call or construction.
deviations: Uses actual Engine oldest-ready selector with native immediate marker and per-callback tick/Promise checkpoint, not full libuv poll/check/timer phase parity. Existing immediately-ready poll-cache ownership/snapshot gates remain open.

Refed active Node tasks own real Engine interest; unref releases it. Zero-interest return leaves unref tasks owned for later activity. Only-unref pollables behind unresolved unrelated interest fail ERR_SM_NODE_UNREF_ONLY_PENDING rather than blocking forever. A ready immediate may run while another component/request interest exists. This is not Node process-exit semantics.
Timeout refresh is implemented only while active and retains original ALS registration cell; fired/closed reactivation refuses. No new context is fabricated on unref/ref/active refresh.
Timeout inactive hasRef retains reference-policy flag like Node; inactive Immediate ref cannot revive it. Active methods always change/query native interest.
setTimeout delay clamps to1..2147483647 and truncates; Node overflow warnings are not emitted. Per-task/private fields, constructor metadata and all exotic coercions are not full Node parity.

Promise timeout/immediate support native AbortSignal, ref option, cancellation and promisify.custom; promise interval async iteration is explicitly deferred. Foreign structural signals/general Scheduler receiver metadata are outside scope.
Mutable CJS objects are shared. Named ESM references capture initial bindings; syncBuiltinESMExports is not implemented.
Existing strict fatal/discard policy remains; no Node uncaught-exception recovery, DEBUG/OOM/reset/GC-pressure or custom host service is introduced.
